title: Hydrogen adsorption properties of in-situ synthesized Pt-decorated porous carbons templated from zeolite EMC-2
material_description: CEMC | plain microporous carbon templated from zeolite EMC-2 by CVD of acetonitrile (acetonitrile/Ar flow) at 1023 K for 3 h; zeolite removed with HF and HCl
purification_method: zeolite template removed by washing with 10% HF several times and refluxing in concentrated HCl at 333 K; dried at 393 K overnight
source_location: main p.11 Table 1 (H2 uptake, footnote b: 77 K and 20 bar), also text p.15; plotted point: Fig. 7 left (p.18) main panel 77 K series, highest-pressure marker (same run as Fig. 6 left CEMC-ad)
notes: digitized: 20.11356932153392 bar, 6.338079470198675 wt%, archive: fig7_77K_CEMC.json. In Fig. 6 left the CEMC-ad marker at 20 bar is hidden under the open CEMC-de marker. isotherm_point_count approximate (16 adsorption markers in Fig. 7 plus 13 identified desorption markers and about 2 partly hidden low-pressure markers in Fig. 6). Table 1 values used; text p.9 gives total pore volume 1.91 cm3 g-1 (Table 1: 1.71). NLDFT pore size distribution (Fig. 2B) centred at around 1.1 and 2.0 nm with majority at 1.1 nm; 1.1 nm stored as modal pore diameter. BET range: 0.02-0.22 (P/P0). Degassing printed as: evacuated to 10^-10 bar and kept at 523 K overnight (duration not numeric, left empty). H2 by Hiden IGA-003 gravimetric analyser; paper states the isotherms were evaluated with the 'measured bulk density of 1.5 g cm-3 for the samples' and an adsorbed-H2 density of 0.04 g/cm3 for buoyancy correction (1.5 stored as skeletal_density_g_cm3 because it is the sample density used for the buoyancy correction; the paper calls it bulk density). Basis never named: uptake_type unspecified; basis_inferred excess by the gravimetric-with-buoyancy-correction default (the correction for adsorbed-phase volume may move values toward absolute). Total pore volume from N2 adsorbed at P/P0 ca. 0.99; micropore area and volume (values in parentheses in Table 1) by t-plot.
